correctness.rationale: Counting shows only distinct line-line pairs can fail to permute, and such a pair permutes exactly when its unique span is a Lie-subalgebra plane, yielding sd(L)=1-q(q+1)(N-t)/(N+t+2)^2. The factorization count follows independently by incidence types. Solvable algebras reduce to projective eigenlines of a 2x2 action. For perfect algebras the bracket matrix is invertible symmetric; its projective isotropic locus has q+1 points both in odd characteristic (nonsingular conic) and characteristic two (a nonzero squared linear form).
